item.title: Digital image analysis-based quantification of p53 immunohistochemistry in gastric cancer: a systematic comparison of three-tier cutoff-derivation strategies in tissue microarrays
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Digital p53 IHC quantification was reproducible at each observer-dependent step. The extended Youden and VUS criteria performed equivalently; therefore, we propose Youden as a reasonable default, pending validation and TP53 correlation.

item.title: Corrigendum to: Preventive Effects of Probiotic Formula on Metabolic Stress Associated Physical Fatigue in Forced Swimming and LPS-Induced Mouse Models
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Integrating DWI Parameters with RECIST 1.1 for Early Assessment of Systemic Therapy Response in Lung Cancer Pelvic Bone Metastases
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Integrating ADC-derived DWI metrics with RECIST 1.1 may provide complementary information for early assessment of pelvic bone metastases from lung cancer, particularly in lesions categorised as stable disease.

item.title: Fluctuating together over time: Within-dyad life satisfaction dynamics in parent-adolescent dyads
item.description: Empirical research has consistently documented positive associations between parents' and adolescents' life satisfaction. However, most evidence is based on between-family designs, leaving within-dyad dynamic processes poorly understood. Using six annual waves of data from 2243 parent-adolescent dyads participating in the Korean Children and Youth Panel Survey (ages 14-19), this study examined whether parents' and adolescents' life satisfaction fluctuates together and predicts subsequent changes...

item.title: Global, regional, and national burden of motor neuron diseases, 1990-2021: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021
item.description: CONCLUSION: From 1990 to 2021, the absolute burden of MNDs increased, age-standardized prevalence and incidence rates declined slightly, and mortality-related burden increased. These trends underscore the need for evidence-based national and global healthcare planning. Geographic variation in MND burden may reflect regional differences in the roles of sociodemographic and genetic factors.

item.title: Psoas-lumbar vertebral index and short-term pain relief after pulsed radiofrequency treatment of the dorsal root ganglion in postherpetic neuralgia in Korea: a retrospective pilot study
item.description: CONCLUSION: This pilot cohort showed no detectable association between PLVI and short-term pain relief after pRF; its small size precludes establishing the absence of an association. The exploratory sex difference warrants investigation in larger prospective studies with comprehensive sarcopenia assessment.

item.title: Masseter Muscle Volume and Cross-Sectional Area as Risk Factors for Late Mechanical Dental Implant Failure: A Matched Case-Control Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Greater masseter muscle volume and CSA were significantly associated with late mechanical implant failure in this matched case-control study. The proposed cut-off values may provide preliminary reference values for risk stratification. However, these findings should be regarded as exploratory and require prospective validation in independent cohorts before routine clinical implementation.

item.title: A Terpene Preparation for the Pharmacological Prevention of Common Bile Duct Stone Recurrence after Endoscopic Clearance: A Randomized Pilot Trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this pilot trial, no CBD stone recurrence occurred in the treatment group despite a numerically higher baseline anatomic risk, whereas two of 12 control-group patients experienced recurrence. The trial was not powered to detect a treatment effect; therefore, no conclusions regarding efficacy can be drawn. The primary contribution is to inform the feasibility and design of a confirmatory trial. (cris.nih.go.kr, KCT0002289).

item.title: Nationwide Claims-Based Incidence and Associated Factors of Adverse Events after Gastric Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide population-based claims study, claims-defined AEs after standard-indication gastric ESD were associated with patient-level and institution-level variables available in administrative data (cris.nih.go.kr, KCT0011604).
item.category: Korea University, Kyung Hee University, SNU

item.title: SFPQ/S100A8 complex induces filaggrin deficiency via selective autophagy and JNK phosphorylation in atopic dermatitis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that the formation of SFPQ/S100A8 complex is a critical process in AD progression, which provides key insights into the pathogenic mechanisms of AD. The elucidation of the SFPQ/S100A8 complex axis in AD pathogenesis can be leveraged to develop therapeutic drugs for AD treatment.

item.title: Efficient genome editing in ASC-derived porcine lung organoids via GFP-guided enrichment
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The PLOs and genome-editing platform developed in this study provide a powerful resource for translational medicine. By enabling precise genetic manipulation in a model that closely mimics human lung physiology, this system offers an essential platform for recapitulating human lung pathologies, studying zoonotic infectious diseases, and validating the efficacy of gene therapies.

item.title: Efficacy of anterioposterior weight-shift training with visual biofeedback for step length asymmetry and functional mobility in chronic stroke: a randomized controlled trial
item.description: CONCLUSION: AP training may effectively improve step length asymmetry and paretic limb mechanics in patients with chronic stroke. By enhancing the anterior weight transfer and propulsive force, this intervention offers a targeted strategy for addressing established asymmetric gait patterns in the chronic phase of recovery. Trial details ClinicalTrial.gov Identifier NCT02207933.

item.title: Longitudinal recovery of physical function after lung transplantation: a comparative analysis of ECMO and non-ECMO recipients
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: LT recipients showed significant improvement in physical function between 6 and 12 months after transplantation. ECMO-bridged recipients had lower independent ambulation rates at 6 months, while no statistically significant between-group difference was observed at 12 months. Further studies incorporating pretransplant and early postoperative assessments are needed to better characterize functional recovery after lung transplantation.

item.title: PlasmaLyte, Lactated Ringer's, or Normal Saline resuscitation in acute pancreatitis: a single-center, pragmatic, cluster-randomized trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this small pragmatic trial, PL, LR, and NS showed no significant difference in the primary clinical endpoint. However, balanced crystalloids were associated with more favorable acid-base profiles than NS. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger multicenter trials with appropriate cluster-adjusted or individually randomized designs.

item.title: Causal effect estimation for ordinal outcomes: a performance comparison of G-computation, IPW, and TMLE-based methods
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Under the specific data-generating mechanisms considered in this study, threshold-based TMLE demonstrated relatively stable performance for estimating the average treatment effect with ordinal outcomes, particularly under single-model misspecification scenarios. Threshold-based TMLE implemented using the Super Learner library performed comparably to its parametric counterpart. In the real-data analysis, methods based on the Super Learner library tended to produce smaller standard...

item.title: Comparison of robotic and laparoscopic gastrectomy using textbook oncologic outcome: a matched cohort study
item.description: By evaluating whether a patient simultaneously satisfies multiple desirable goals, textbook oncologic outcome (TOO) offers a composite assessment of cancer-surgery quality. This study investigated whether TOO attainment after curative gastric cancer surgery differed according to the operative approach. We retrospectively reviewed 945 patients with gastric adenocarcinoma who received curative-intent robotic gastrectomy (RG; n = 161) or laparoscopic gastrectomy (LG; n = 784) between 2017 and 2025....

item.title: Current role of boron neutron capture therapy in head and neck cancer: insights from 4 years of clinical experience
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: BNCT should be administered during the early disease stages when no other effective treatment options are available. Further studies should determine the factors contributing to treatment efficacy and safety, thereby optimizing multimodal treatment strategies involving BNCT.

item.title: Clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction following implant removal after open wedge high tibial osteotomy
item.description: CONCLUSION: Implant removal after OWHTO was associated with improvements in pain, clinical scores, and patient satisfaction. Furthermore, the frequency of complications after implant removal was very low. These findings suggest that implant removal after OWHTO may be beneficial.

item.title: Establishment of age- and sex-stratified normative data for the Brief Assessment of Cognition (BAC) app in healthy Japanese individuals
item.description: The Brief Assessment of Cognition in Schizophrenia (BACS) and its Japanese version are widely used instruments for the brief and efficient assessment of cognitive domains commonly impaired in schizophrenia. A tablet-administered version, the Brief Assessment of Cognition (BAC) App, has been developed; however, normative data for the BAC App have not yet been established for the general Japanese population. This cross-sectional study aimed to establish normative data for the Japanese version of...

item.title: Gender-based discrimination shapes psychological safety and professional identity in clinical settings: a qualitative study of nursing, midwifery, and medical students
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that gender-responsive and psychologically safe clinical learning environments may be important across nursing, midwifery, and medical education. Educators, supervisors, and clinical staff should consider addressing gendered role labelling, inequitable task allocation, and hidden curricula as potential structural barriers to learning and participation. Transparent and auditable learning objectives, gender-responsive supervision, monitoring of task and feedback...

item.title: A 2-pyrone-4,6-dicarboxylic acid biosensor for lignin valorization based on a newly identified transcriptional regulatory system
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: ΔligI(pCup1) enables real-time, specific detection of PDC produced from lignin-derived aromatic compounds, including those in black liquor extract derived from lignocellulosic biomass, demonstrating applicability to screening for lignin valorization. Integration of this biosensor with diverse strain engineering approaches, including random mutagenesis, adaptive laboratory evolution, and metagenomics-based enzyme discovery, would provide a platform for efficient selection of SYK-6...

item.title: Risk factors for surgical site infection requiring reoperation after osteotomy around the knee: a multicenter retrospective study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative skin disease, preoperative liver disease, and postoperative hemoglobin decline were independently associated with an increased risk of SSI requiring reoperation after OAK. Awareness of these factors may aid perioperative risk assessment and postoperative surveillance. Further prospective studies with larger cohorts are needed to validate these findings and establish clinically applicable strategies for infection risk assessment and prevention.

item.title: Digital self-management application for patients undergoing hemodialysis: influences on health awareness and frailty
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This pilot feasibility study suggests that digital self-management applications may influence health awareness and selected patient-centered outcomes in HD patients, particularly psychological aspects of frailty. Larger controlled multicenter studies are needed to further evaluate the long-term clinical and psychosocial effects of digital health interventions in dialysis care.

item.title: Access Vessel Patency After Endovascular Therapy via Tibiopedal Access in Patients With Lower Extremity Artery Disease
item.description: CONCLUSION: The present study demonstrated a relatively high incidence of loss of access vessel patency after endovascular therapy via tibiopedal access, although this was not associated with an increase in major adverse limb events. A larger sheath-to-artery ratio was identified as an independent predictor of loss of access vessel patency.

item.title: Integrating microbial fermentation and polymerization for sustainable polylactic acid production
item.description: Replacing petroleum-based plastics with sustainable alternatives requires economically viable biomanufacturing routes. This review comprehensively assimilates two critical pillars of bio-based polymer development: the microbial synthesis of lactic acid (LA) and its subsequent polymerization into polylactic acid (PLA). The first section critically examines advancements in the eco-friendly production of LA from renewable substrates through microbial fermentation. It highlights recent breakthroughs...

item.title: Factors associated with serum GDF-15, iron deficiency and lower hemoglobin levels in patients with chronic heart failure and healthy elderly people
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Lower hemoglobin levels in patients with heart failure might be associated with elevated serum GDF-15 due to higher serum NT-proBNP and inflammation, as well as iron deficiency. In contrast, lower hemoglobin levels in healthy elderly individuals might involve lower serum iron and hepcidin levels. Lower serum iron concentration was suggested to be involved in left atrial remodeling in patients with heart failure.

item.title: Integrated metabolomics and microbiome analyses reveal nutritional differences between yellow and white maize (Zea mays L.) kernels
item.description: Maize (Zea mays L.) is a globally significant cereal crop that exhibits wide phenotypic and nutritional diversity. Yellow maize is highly valued for its accumulation of health-promoting carotenoids, whereas the functional profile of white maize is characterized by distinct classes of secondary metabolites. However, the complex interplay among host genetics, the kernel endophytic microbiome, and the associated metabolic profiles remains poorly understood. In this study, we employed an integrated...

item.title: Development and preliminary psychometric evaluation of a spectacle trial-wear questionnaire for distance single-vision prescriptions
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: ASTWES is a concise candidate questionnaire with preliminary evidence of a correlated three-domain structure, acceptable internal consistency, and short-term clinical association in Chinese adults aged 18-35 years. Further independent patient-centered content evaluation and external validation are needed before routine use or fixed decision thresholds are considered.

item.title: Patient-Reported Outcomes Following Two-Tined Three-Site Conventional Radiofrequency Ablation of Genicular Nerves for Chronic Knee Pain
item.description: CONCLUSION: In this real-world cohort, conventional GNRFA using the classical three-site technique demonstrated robust short-term pain reduction, and at least half of the cohort maintained clinically meaningful pain improvements for 11 months. For chronic knee pain, GNRFA is a reasonable therapeutic option in appropriately selected patients.

item.title: Multi-omics profiling reveals molecular features of visceral adiposity in autonomous cortisol secretion
item.description: Autonomous cortisol secretion (ACS) from adrenal adenomas increases cardiometabolic risk. Visceral adiposity is a hallmark of ACS. We characterized ACS-associated visceral adiposity using multi-omics profiling of periadrenal adipose tissue and plasma. ACS exhibited higher visceral-to-subcutaneous fat ratio (VSR), adipocyte hypertrophy, and inflammation-related pathway enrichment than non-functioning adrenal tumors. RNA-seq deconvolution and immunohistochemistry indicated increased macrophage...

item.title: Implementation of a nonprofit specialty clinic for vascular anomalies and birthmarks in Vietnam: A 12-year service evaluation
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Limited global awareness of invasive alien species and little support for their management
item.description: Invasive alien species (IAS) are one of the main drivers of global change and can cause a wide range of negative ecological and social impacts. Addressing these impacts requires management actions, which can fail to be effective when not supported by the public. Here, we conducted the first global survey on people's awareness and perceptions of IAS and support for their management. Our results revealed low public awareness and understanding of biological invasions, and suggest that these are...

item.title: Food and dietary supplement expenditures associated with dietary self-management among women with endometriosis: A cross-sectional study in Hungary
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Endometriosis is associated with greater financial burden from dietary self-management. These findings highlight the need for evidence-based nutritional guidance and consideration of economic impact in care.

item.title: Validation and modification of a Chinese smell identification test (CSIT-12) in patients with Parkinson's disease and rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the discriminative value of utilizing culturally familiar odors for the screening of PD and RBD in Chinese populations. Furthermore, the abbreviated odor subsets offer highly efficient, rapid screening options suitable for community-based testing and fast-paced clinical environments.

item.title: Social determinants of partner and non-partner sexual violence against women in Chile: a population-based multilevel analysis
item.description: BACKGROUND: Sexual violence against women is a major public health problem in Latin America, yet evidence on its social determinants is scarce and often conflates partner and non-partner forms. We characterised determinants of intimate partner sexual violence (IPSV), non-partner sexual assault (NPSA), and non-partner sexual harassment (NPSH) in Chile and compared their risk profiles.

item.title: Short- and long-term effects of dronedarone on Cav3.1- and Cav3.2-T-type calcium channel current
item.description: T-type calcium channels (TTCCs), including the Cav3.1 and Cav3.2 subtypes, play a critical role in regulating cardiac electrical activity. Their abnormal expression is closely associated with arrhythmias and cardiac dysfunction caused by myocardial infarction (MI). Dronedarone, a multi-target antiarrhythmic drug, is widely used to treat atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter but has shown adverse effects under pathological conditions such as MI. This study aims to investigate the direct effects...

item.title: Construction of electrostatic binding V-type starches using cationic starch and lauric acid: Insight into enhanced digestive resistance
item.description: This study developed a V-type starch with enhanced structural stability and digestive resistance through an electrostatic interaction between a cationic starch (CS) and lauric acid (LA). X-ray diffraction analysis revealed that the non-etherified sample complexed with LA (ETA-0%-LA) exhibits a typical B-type crystalline structure. When the ETA content was increased from 5% to 30%, the V-type crystallinity of the CS-LA complexes increased from 9.22% to 24.60%. The degree of substitution (DS)...

item.title: Flavored e-cigarette use and its association with subsequent short-term e-cigarette abstinence among youth, young adults and adults: Findings from the United States longitudinal population assessment of tobacco use and health, 2016 to 2023
item.description: AIMS: This study examined e-cigarette flavor use and its prospective association with short-term e-cigarette abstinence among youth (12-17 years old), young adults (18-24 years old) and adults (25+ years old) using United States (US)-representative data.

item.title: Advances and challenges in inner ear drug delivery: limitations and therapeutic perspectives
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Hearing loss is a major global health burden, with age-related hearing loss affecting hundreds of millions of people worldwide. Despite significant therapeutic advances, effective treatment remains hampered by the challenge of delivering drugs to the inner ear, an anatomically inaccessible and tightly protected organ.

item.title: Retrospective evaluation of first-trimester miscarriage following euploid embryo transfer
item.description: CONCLUSION: Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy appears effective; the majority of firsttrimester miscarriages after euploid embryo transfers are unlikely to be explained by discordant PGT-A results. Despite its high accuracy, PGT-A cannot detect all forms of chromosomal mosaicism and therefore cannot completely prevent miscarriage. Reviews of clinical and medical histories, along with cytogenetic testing of POG after a miscarriage following euploid embryo transfer in selected cases,...

item.title: Aging in Autism: An Event-Related Potentials Study of Auditory Change Detection
item.description: Autistic individuals are often thought to exhibit reduced tolerance for change, which may stem from atypicalities in sensory processing, particularly in the detection of environmental changes. Within the predictive coding framework, this intolerance may reflect altered generation and updating internal predictions in response to sensory input, leading to increased prediction errors. Mismatch negativity and the P3a component are event-related potentials (ERPs) indexing automatic auditory change...

item.title: Genomic insights into trichome and inflorescence evolution of the palaeopolyploid tree genus Greyia
item.description: The southern African endemic tree Greyia Hook. & Harv. (Francoaceae, Geraniales) comprises three species distinguished by striking variation in trichome morphology and inflorescence architecture, yet the genomic and regulatory basis of these traits has remained largely unexplored. Here, we present chromosome-scale genome assemblies for all recognised Greyia species, namely Greyia radlkoferi, Greyia sutherlandii, and Greyia flanaganii, providing the first high-quality genomic resources for...

item.title: A WSI-Independent Inference Framework for Cervical and Urinary Cytology Using Hierarchical Labels
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: CYTOLONE-v2 demonstrates the technical feasibility of extending a hierarchical cytology classification framework from cervical to urinary cytology. The findings are limited to selected WSI-derived fields and a Reactive change-versus-Urothelial carcinoma test cohort; external, case-level, direct-microscopy and prospective workflow validation is required before clinical utility can be established.

item.title: Boosting Male Participation in Research: Exploring Motivation, Engagement, and Retention Efforts
item.description: CONCLUSION: Gender-sensitive, equity-informed approaches are essential for engaging males, particularly those from underrepresented groups, in longitudinal research. Strategies addressing masculinity norms, socioeconomic context, and institutional trust will strengthen the diversity and generalizability of observational study findings.

item.title: Effects of Aerobic Exercise on Autonomic and Endothelial Function and Splanchnic Hemodynamics in Compensated Cirrhosis: RCT Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: AE is safe and effectively improves functional capacity in compensated cirrhosis. However, positive signals in autonomic and hepatic parameters were not between-group significant, necessitating a cautious interpretation.

item.title: Carbon Accumulation in Tropical Dry Forests and Savannas Despite Widespread Land-Cover Change, Revealed by Radar Remote Sensing
item.description: Accurate mapping of woody biomass and its temporal change is critical for understanding the global carbon balance, informing restoration and supporting evidence-based policy on climate mitigation and livelihoods. The vegetation of the dry tropics, comprised largely of dry forests and savannas, holds substantial woody carbon stocks, but both stocks and change over time remain uncertain. Where Earth Observation (EO) data have been used to estimate change over time, different products give...

item.title: Resilience Through Connection: A Group Coaching Framework for Women Anesthesiologists in the Women's Empowerment and Leadership Initiative (WELI)
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Results of this pilot intervention suggest group coaching programs for anesthesiologists have the potential to build resilience in the current work environment, thereby benefiting not only individuals but the anesthesiology workforce as a whole.

item.title: Anti-breast Cancer Potential of Prosopis cineraria L. Phytocompounds: A Network Pharmacology and in vitro Analysis based Approach
item.description: CONCLUSION: Network analysis exhibited that PCL exerted a significant repressive impact on BCa by acting on tumor-associated signaling cascade, which would be helpful for future anticancer research of PCL against breast cancer.

item.title: Neurofeedback for Management of Musculoskeletal Pain: A Randomized Control Trial Using DOMS
item.description: CONCLUSION: A single neurofeedback session was insufficient to modulate brain activity or pain perception. Methodological factors, including limited training duration and participants' strategies, may have contributed to the lack of an observable effect.

item.title: Cognitive Functions and Gene Polymorphism Associated with Cardiovascular Risk in Young Adults vs. Patients with Arterial Hypertension
item.description: CONCLUSION: It should be noted that polymorphic variants of genes involved in lipid metabolism and antioxidant defense-namely, the -482 C>T variant of the APOC3 gene and the L55M A>T variant of the PON1 gene-are significantly associated with lower cognitive test scores in young individuals. The genetic analysis, including the determination of the Q192R A>G polymorphism of the PON1 gene and the -482 C>T polymorphism of the APOC3 gene, may be included in the examination of patients with arterial...

item.title: Expanding Patient Choice in Diabetes Care: Reducing Access Barriers to Inhaled Insulin
item.description: Inhaled insulin provides a unique prandial insulin option, offering an alternative, with a more rapid onset of effect, to subcutaneous rapid-acting analog insulin. Clinical studies with inhaled insulin have demonstrated its efficacy and safety, with glycemic outcomes comparable to or in some cases better than those of contemporary insulin delivery approaches. However, the use of inhaled insulin for diabetes therapy in daily life remains limited due to payer restrictions, prior authorization...

item.title: Similar Long-Term Incidence of Hepatocellular Carcinoma in Chronic Hepatitis B Initiating Entecavir Versus Tenofovir Alafenamide: A REAL-B Study
item.description: Data on potential differences in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) incidence between entecavir (ETV) and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients are limited. This retrospective multinational study included treatment-naïve adults with CHB without a history of HCC who initiated ETV or TAF therapy since 2016 at 23 centres in 4 countries. Baseline characteristics were balanced using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and propensity score matching (PSM). HCC...

item.title: Premature treatment cessation in pediatric acute myeloid leukemia due to excessive toxicity: clinical experiences and patient outcomes - a case series
item.description: Although survival in pediatric acute myeloid leukemia (AML) has improved over the past decades, intensive chemotherapy may be associated with severe and life-threatening toxicities. This case series describes pediatric AML patients in whom therapy was discontinued due to excessive toxicity. Patients were identified through a national database of two consecutive AML treatment protocols in the Netherlands (2010-2023). Seven patients were included; discontinuation of treatment was because of a...

item.title: Neuronal Overexpression of Glycogen Synthase Kinase-3β Accelerates Age-Related Glial, Vascular, and Inflammatory Remodeling of the Murine Dentate Gyrus
item.description: Adult hippocampal neurogenesis (AHN)-the lifelong generation of new neurons in the dentate gyrus (DG)-depends on the integrity of the subgranular zone (SGZ) neurogenic niche, which comprises astrocytes, microglia, oligodendroglial cells, and a dense vascular network. Although AHN declines during aging and is impaired in Alzheimer's disease (AD), the cell-type-specific alterations within the DG underlying this decline remain poorly characterized. Given the critical role of glycogen synthase...

item.title: Evolving new signals from conserved protein scaffolds
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Turning Red to Green Repeatedly: Ancestral LWS Duplications Drive Convergent Visual Tuning in Teleost Fishes
item.description: Photopigments, formed by an opsin protein bound to a light-sensitive chromophore, underlie vertebrate vision. Long-wavelength-sensitive (LWS) opsins mediate red-light detection, and most teleosts retain a single functional LWS1. A shorter-shifted green-sensitive paralog (LWS2) is found only in a few lineages. By mining teleost genomes and sequencing retinal transcriptomes, we identify elopomorphs as an additional lineage retaining LWS2 (alongside characins and osteoglossomorphs). Surprisingly,...

item.title: Livelihoods after resettlement: women's work, collective care, and solidarity in disaster recovery
item.description: This paper critically examines livelihood recovery in the peripheral resettlement sites of Chennai, India, following the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami. Despite the implementation of various gender-inclusive livelihood programmes as a part of disaster recovery, our longitudinal empirical research reveals a persistent gap between formal recovery measures and the everyday conditions required for livelihoods to become gender-inclusive and sustainable over time. Drawing on in-depth fieldwork, we explore...

item.title: Interfacial Regulation via Organic-Inorganic Interpenetrating Networks for Enhanced Protection in Waterborne Polyurethane Nanocomposites
item.description: The abundance of hydrophilic groups and the linear polymer chain structure in waterborne polyurethane (WPU) lead to insufficient water resistance and corrosion protection. These inherent characteristics make it challenging for WPU to be applied in the marine protection field, where high comprehensive performance of coatings is demanded. Herein, a WPU nanocomposite was designed incorporating hydroxyl-terminated polydimethylsiloxane and bifunctionalized nano-silica (modified with...

item.title: An Echocardiogram-Based Ultrasound Radiomic Model Predicts Recovery of Coronary Artery Diameter in Kawasaki Disease
item.description: CONCLUSION: Machine learning models can predict the recovery of coronary artery diameter in KD and thus may offer important value for clinical decision-making.

item.title: From Innovation to Translation: Emerging Direct-Analysis Mass Spectrometry Platforms
item.description: Ambient and direct-analysis mass spectrometry has shifted from predominantly proof-of-concept rapid screening to increasingly robust analytical platforms with clearer translational potential. This focused critical review examines the following four emerging or strategically relevant platforms: dielectric-barrier-discharge ionization (DBDI), liquid electron ionization (LEI), paper cone spray ionization (PCSI), and sandpaper spray ionization (SPS). DBDI, PCSI, and SPS are ambient or ambient-like...

item.title: Offense and Victim Characteristics of Veteran Violent Offenses: Insights From the 2016 Survey of Prison Inmates
item.description: Previous research highlights critical Veteran-civilian differences in antisocial behavior, including unique demographic and offense characteristics among justice-involved Veterans and disproportionately high involvement of Veterans in family violence. However, comparatively limited empirical attention has investigated potential victim characteristics of Veterans with criminal-legal involvement, resulting in a limited understanding of these Veterans' criminogenic and rehabilitative needs. Using a...

item.title: An Exploratory Study on the Onset Age of Child Sexual Abuse: A Comparison of Childhood and Adolescence Onset
item.description: Research on child sexual abuse has predominantly focused on cases that typically begin in early childhood. By contrast, sexual abuse and boundary violations that first occur during adolescence have received comparatively little attention. This study aims to analyze the similarities and differences in the age of abuse onset in childhood and adolescence, considering victim characteristics and abuse-related factors. The study is based on anonymously collected data from the German Sexual Abuse...

item.title: Promoting inclusivity and partnership with recipients of health services: short report on redesigning Engaging All Voices (previously Consumer Voice)
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: We sampled people from multiple service settings and thus, findings may generalize in healthcare, education, carceral, and other systems. Our experience redesigning Engaging All Voices revealed that how recipients of innovations are referred to can shape receptiveness to engagement approaches. There is no single "right" term to refer to service users across settings. Engaging All Voices now guides learners in an early exercise to determine terminology preferred by service users...

item.title: Evaluation of the OPTESK VR training simulator for gastric bleeding treatment
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: OPTESK can serve as a valuable training tool for endoscopic treatment of bleeding in the upper GI tract. This approach may help reduce dependence on animal-based training and enable risk-free practice prior to clinical intervention.

item.title: Metabolic processes and microenvironmental regulation in leukemia
item.description: Leukemia, a heterogeneous group of hematologic malignancies, continues to present significant therapeutic challenges owing to persistent issues, such as relapse, drug resistance, and treatment-related toxicity. While traditional research has primarily focused on genetic drivers, there is increasing recognition of the critical roles played by the bone marrow microenvironment (BMME) and metabolic reprogramming in disease pathogenesis. This review systematically elucidates the dynamic interplay...

item.title: A Genome-Wide Meta-Analysis of Functional Dyspepsia in 1,168,899 Individuals Implicates Immune Pathways in Disease Susceptibility
item.description: CONCLUSIONS & INFERENCES: This study implicates immune-driven pathways in FD susceptibility, adds insights into the pathophysiological mechanisms of the disease, and reveals DHX36 as a candidate target for future investigation.

item.title: The Japanese Adaptation of the Reading the Mind in Films Test: Differentiating Autism Spectrum Disorder From Depression Using an Ecologically Valid Social Cognitive Task
item.description: Cognitive tests that reflect the complexity of real-world social interactions are essential for autism spectrum disorder (ASD)-related clinical assessment and research. This study developed and adapted a Japanese version of the Reading the Mind in Films (RMF) test, which assesses mind-reading ability through dynamic, multisensory, and context-rich stimuli. Participants included 23 autistic adults, 39 typically developing adults, and 40 adults with depression as a clinical control. RMF scores in...

item.title: Screen use, parent-child interaction, and social interaction behaviors in autistic children
item.description: The rapid expansion of digital technologies has transformed children's everyday environments, raising concerns about excessive screen use and its potential developmental implications. Although research on screen use has increased substantially, relatively little is known about how screen use may relate to family interaction processes among autistic children. The present study aimed to examine the relationships among screen use, autism severity, parent-child interaction behaviors, and children's...

item.title: Exome-wide association study reveals common and rare coding variants shaping chronic pain in 327,642 UK biobank participants
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide a comprehensive map of coding variation underlying chronic pain and show that both common and rare coding variants contribute to its genetic architecture. Rare coding variants explain only a limited fraction of heritability but offer strong mechanistic insight by implicating discrete genes and pathways related to neuronal development, neuroimmune signaling, and tissue homeostasis. This work advances understanding of chronic pain biology and provides a...

item.title: COL10A1<sup>+</sup> fibroblasts define rupture-prone abdominal aortic aneurysms and enable molecular risk stratification
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies a COL10A1^(+) fibroblast-associated transcriptional state that defines a rupture-prone vascular microenvironment in abdominal aortic aneurysm. The derived COL10A1-IGFBP6 signature establishes a biologically informed framework for molecular risk stratification, complementing anatomical size-based assessment and providing a foundation for future development of mechanism-guided strategies to refine AAA risk evaluation.

item.title: Molecular detection and characterization of Anaplasma marginale in cattle from the Lower Shabelle Region of Somalia
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study confirms the high prevalence and genetic diversity of A. marginale in Somali cattle, highlighting the need for improved surveillance and control measures.

item.title: Trimester-specific associations of maternal vitamin D metabolic markers with risks of small vulnerable newborns: a prospective birth cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Trimester-specific vitamin D metabolic profiles showed differential associations with neonatal risks, with stronger corrected evidence for adverse associations related to epimerization-derived markers than for early inverse associations of conventional 25(OH)D metabolites. These findings support comprehensive vitamin D metabolic monitoring and further investigation of tailored supplementation strategies to improve maternal-fetal health.

item.title: Self-cascade oxygen-generating hydrogel/nanofibrous membrane composites restore periodontal microenvironment homeostasis
item.description: The hypoxic environment of deep periodontal pockets favors the thriving of anaerobic microbes, leading to dysbiosis, tissue destruction, and treatment resistance. Elevating intra-pocket oxygen tension is a fundamental yet unmet need for controlling anaerobic pathogens in deep periodontal pockets. Our previous study demonstrated the therapeutic efficacy of oxygen-releasing hydrogel based on calcium peroxide (CPO) in reducing anaerobic pathogens in vitro. However, the rapid hydrolysis of...

item.title: Quantitative proteomic landscape reveals the role of CSPG5 in the recurrence of glioma
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: CSPG5 acts as a novel suppressor of ErbB2 signaling; its loss facilitates ErbB2 hyperactivation and thereby promotes glioma recurrence.

item.title: Development and validation of the synthetic index of palliative care integration into primary health care
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The SIPCI provides a reproducible, system-level measure for monitoring and benchmarking territorial patterns of palliative care integration within primary health care in Colombia. The findings describe marked geographic heterogeneity and support the use of SIPCI for routine monitoring and planning, without implying causal mechanisms or patient-level effects. Although the index showed good internal coherence and robustness, further studies may help strengthen its construct validity...

item.title: Public brain health: a framework for action to promote and safeguard brain health
item.description: The promotion of brain health has generally been undertaken at the level of individuals, for instance, in the quest for precision treatments for persons with, or at high risk of, neurological disorders. But the growing global burden of neurological conditions and the increasing understanding of the brain's central role in all facets of human life have spurred interest in public health approaches to the brain that emphasise population-level strategies benefitting everyone as part of a "brain...

item.title: Single‑cell and spatial transcriptomics in chronic lung disease: cellular heterogeneity and molecular mechanisms in IPF and COPD
item.description: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) have advanced the study of complex lung diseases by resolving cellular heterogeneity, tissue architecture, and intercellular communication. These technologies are particularly informative in chronic respiratory disorders, where pathological remodeling involves coordinated alterations across epithelial, stromal, immune, and endothelial compartments. Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), a rare fatal fibrotic disorder, and...

item.title: Duration of untreated illness in eating disorders: a comprehensive systematic review and meta-regression
item.description: CONCLUSION: Individuals with EDs experience substantial delays before accessing treatment, with untreated illness exceeding 20 months on average. Older age was associated with longer DUED, suggesting potential gaps in detection and help-seeking among adults. DUED varies across demographic, geographic and methodological factors. While decreasing DUED over time is encouraging, these findings highlight the need for earlier identification and streamlined care pathways to reduce delays and improve...

item.title: Mapping fibroblast plasticity across non-cancer lung diseases at single-cell resolution
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This work establishes a comprehensive single-cell fibroblast atlas of non-cancer lung diseases, uncovering disease- and subtype-specific regulatory programs and highlighting potential therapeutic targets for fibrotic remodeling.

item.title: Needs among persons with advanced COPD and their informal caregivers: a multi-perspective qualitative study focusing on the potential role of palliative care
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Persons with advanced COPD and their informal caregivers reported numerous needs. Persons receiving palliative care reported relief from various needs. Timely information about COPD's progression and palliative care could increase acceptance and thus use of palliative care among these persons and could consequently reduce or curtail the burden of living with advanced COPD.

item.title: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy as a tool for monitoring treatment-related neurofunctional changes in posttraumatic stress disorder and trauma-related symptomatology: a narrative review
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence suggests that fNIRS represents a promising and clinically feasible approach for monitoring treatment-related neurofunctional changes in PTSD and trauma-related symptomatology, particularly during non-pharmacological interventions targeting prefrontal regulatory processes. Rather than replacing established neuroimaging techniques such as functional magnetic resonance imaging, fNIRS should be considered a complementary tool that is particularly suitable for repeated...

item.title: AKAP2/PKA complex coordinates primary ciliogenesis, ciliary trafficking and Shh signaling
item.description: The primary cilium is a sensory organelle present in all eukaryotic cells that acts as a signaling hub that receives, integrates and transmits signals carried out by extracellular stimuli, playing a fundamental role in cell behavior, development and tissue homeostasis. Genetic mutations in genes encoding for structural components and regulators of primary cilium underlie severe developmental defects, also known as ciliopathies. Understanding cilium biology may, thus, provide novel therapeutic...

item.title: Defining optimal treatment strategies for nasopharyngeal carcinoma based on the ninth edition TNM staging system: insights from a multicenter cohort study in an endemic region
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Under the TNM-9, management recommendations were as follows: radical IMRT alone for stage IA; CCRT for stage IB and T3N0; and high-intensity therapy for high-risk disease, including reclassified subsets. For metastatic disease, the addition of LRRT and MT to systemic therapy was associated with improved survival in both M1a and M1b patients, whereas a trend toward potential benefit from LCT was observed only in M1a subgroup.

item.title: Associations between gastrointestinal symptoms and coexisting symptoms amongst patients in a palliative care unit: a PCOC-based longitudinal study
item.description: CONCLUSION: GI symptoms in hospice ward patients are closely linked to coexisting symptoms, functional status, clinician-rated problem severity, and palliative care phase, and should not be assessed in isolation. Daily standardized assessment using the PCOC framework may help support more individualized symptom management for palliative care patients.

item.title: A risk assessment model for gestational diabetes mellitus integrating maternal demographics and hematological indices in Thai women
item.description: CONCLUSION: The new risk assessment model, which uses basic demographic and routine blood test data, offers a reliable and affordable way to screen for GDM. This method enables early risk identification and helps healthcare providers use resources more efficiently, potentially reducing unnecessary tests in resource-limited settings.

item.title: Comparative evaluation of dentin microcrack formation after root canal preparation with different nickel-titanium instrument systems based on micro-CT: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Within the limitations of this ex vivo meta-analysis, instrument kinematics did not influence microcrack formation, while thermally treated NiTi instruments significantly reduced risk. Thermally treated systems are preferred, and highly flexible, advanced-design instruments should be prioritized for curved canals to minimize dentin microcracks.

item.title: A prognostic model combining hilar lymph node metastasis and preoperative anemia to predict outcomes after curative resection of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The integration of LNM status and preoperative anemia emerges as a novel and clinically valuable prognostic indicator, effectively predicting outcomes in patients with ICC following curative resection, thereby providing tailored clinical guidance for postoperative adjuvant therapy selection and intensive surveillance planning.

item.title: Efgartigimod-responsive autoimmune peripheral neuropathy with concurrent anti-GM2 IgG and anti-contactin-1 IgG antibodies: a rare case report
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of concurrent anti-GM2 IgG and anti-CNTN1 IgG positivity in a single patient. This case describes a previously unrecognized antibody combination in immune-mediated peripheral neuropathy, suggesting a possible overlap of distinct immune-mediated mechanisms. Neonatal Fc receptor blockade may represent a mechanism-based therapeutic option in selected patients with severe or treatment-refractory disease.

item.title: Mapping the interplay of intelligence, empathy, systemizing, and autistic traits in children with and without autism spectrum disorder
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings reveal both shared and distinct patterns of network organization among intelligence, empathy, systemizing, and autistic traits in children with and without ASD. Cognitive empathy may represent a potential target for future intervention research, while systemizing tendencies and cognitive strengths may also inform individualized support strategies in ASD.

item.title: Parabacteroides distasonis ameliorates methylphenidate hydrochloride-induced colonic inflammatory responses and associated gastrointestinal distress
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, this is the first study verifying that P. distasonis supplementation mitigates MPH-induced gastrointestinal adverse reactions, providing a novel intervention strategy to improve tolerance of ADHD pharmacotherapy.

item.title: Decoding radiation-induced transcriptomic signatures of human leukocytes using long-read RNA-seq: clinical and biodosimetric implications
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study is the first to systematically investigate differential transcript usage in the leukocyte fraction of irradiated human whole blood using long-read RNA sequencing. We confirmed known radiation-response signatures at the gene level and identified transcript-level regulatory events and novel candidate isoforms that can be masked in gene-level analyses and conventional short-read pipelines. These findings demonstrate the potential of long-read RNA sequencing to provide a more...

item.title: Automated Magnetic Resonance Volumetry to Measure Multiple System Atrophy Disease Progression in Clinical Trials
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings support longitudinal MRI-derived regional atrophy rates as sensitive imaging endpoints to assess treatment efficacy in MSA clinical trials. © 2026 The Author(s). item.title: Antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of ZnO-NPs against Streptococcus suis serotype 9 in vitro
item.description: Streptococcus suis is an important swine pathogen and an emerging zoonotic threat, with serotype 9 (SS9) increasingly recognized as an important pathogenic serotype. Biofilm formation contributes to the persistence, antimicrobial tolerance, and pathogenicity of S. suis, yet effective strategies for controlling biofilm-associated infections caused by SS9 remain limited. In this study, we evaluated the antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO-NPs) against SS9 and...

item.title: Integrated Spatial and Bulk Transcriptomic Analysis Identifies a Multicellular Ecosystem Involved in Progression of Young Breast Cancer
item.description: Young breast cancer (YBC), defined as diagnosis at or before the age of 40 years, is characterized by an aggressive phenotype and poor prognosis. The tumor microenvironment (TME), comprising immune and stromal cells, plays a critical role in tumor initiation and progression and is closely associated with clinical outcomes. However, alterations in cell states and the organization of multicellular ecosystems within the YBC microenvironment remain poorly understood. We analyzed 7379 bulk...

item.title: Hemodynamic and Geometrical Parameters Associated with Carotid Artery Stenosis: A Cross-Sectional Study Using 4D Flow MRI and CFD
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Carotid geometry carries two complementary signals: markers of disease presence (bifurcation angle, ICA angle) and candidate anatomical substrates of pro-atherogenic flow in still-non-stenosed bifurcations (bulb area, area ratio). Together with the post-stenotic expansion ratio, these geometric features define a compact, image-derivable set of candidate biomarkers for future early carotid risk stratification.

item.title: Decision dynamics of negative bias in subclinical depression during ambiguous facial emotion perception
item.description: Individuals with depressive tendencies may categorize ambiguous facial expressions toward negative rather than happy endpoints, but the associated decision-process components remained unclear. The study examined whether the categorization shift was associated with differences in perceptual criterion, discrimination sensitivity, response dynamics, or diffusion-model parameters. Fifty-nine participants, comprising a depressive tendency group and a comparison group, categorized morphed Sad-Happy...

item.title: BLIX-Ray: Chest X-Ray Report Generation with Vision-Language Models and Reinforcement Learning
item.description: The radiology report is essential for directing the course of treatment for a patient. However, writing radiology reports is a huge burden for radiologists. Manual reporting faces challenges due to intra-labeler and inter-labeler variability, causing inconsistent patient treatment and diagnostic results, and complicating matters due to alertness and changing judgment. To address these challenges, we propose an automated radiology report generation model tailored for chest X-ray imaging. We...

item.title: Artificial intelligent computing of hybrid nano suspension for enhanced thermal mechanism in Jeffery Hamel configuration
item.description: Nanofluids have potential role in the heat transfer enhancement for engineering applications. These fluids together with physical controls change the dynamics of flow inside oblique channel. Thus, this work focuses on the organization of hybrid model using dissipation function and enhanced properties nanoparticles (NiZnFe(2)O(4), and MnZnFe(2)O(4)). The similarity transforms used in the governing model and obtain a new model for hybrid nanofluids. The output estimated in the form of graphical...

item.title: A USP28-TM9SF3-Golgiphagy axis maintains glycosylation homeostasis and promotes breast cancer progression
item.description: Selective autophagy of the Golgi apparatus (Golgiphagy) is essential for Golgi quality control, yet its regulation and physiological functions remain poorly understood. Here, we identify the deubiquitinase USP28 as an upstream regulator of the Golgiphagy receptor TM9SF3. USP28 removes degradative K48-linked ubiquitin chains from TM9SF3, preventing its proteasomal degradation and sustaining Golgiphagy under nutrient and Golgi stresses. item.title: ATP-driven dynamics and itraconazole binding of the drug efflux pump Cdr1 from Candida glabrata
item.description: Azole resistance in Candida species is often caused by the overexpression of Cdr1. Despite its clinical relevance, the structural basis for its ATP-driven efflux pump function remains elusive. We present four high-resolution cryo-EM structures of Candida glabrata Cdr1 obtained in the absence and presence of ATP-Mg²⁺, itraconazole, and vanadate, capturing distinct nucleotide- and substrate-occupancy states. Additional low-population cryo-EM conformers were unveiled by 3D variability analysis,...

item.description: H2AK119ub (H2Aub) and H3K27me3, which are deposited by the Polycomb group (PcG) complexes PRC1 and PRC2, respectively, cooperatively repress developmental genes. However, in human preimplantation embryos, H3K27me3 undergoes genome-wide erasure and subsequent restoration. How H3K27me3 is reestablished and whether PcG complexes still regulate gene repression in human embryos remain unknown. Here, we profiled H2Aub dynamics from human gametes to blastocysts. item.description: No effective treatments currently exist for tauopathies. Given emerging evidence that moderate-dose ionizing radiation (IR) may exert neuroreparative effects in neurodegeneration, we investigated the impact of combined IR exposure on disease progression in the Tau P301S mouse model. Tau P301S mice received combined gamma-ray (0.24 Gy) and carbon-12 nuclei (0.18 Gy, 400 MeV/n) irradiation at the presymptomatic stage. Following longitudinal behavioral testing until the terminal stage, post-mortem...

item.description: Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) are approved for homologous recombination-deficient (HRD) high-grade serous ovarian cancers. However, their durable benefit is severely limited by resistance and hematologic toxicity. PARPi are also largely ineffective in homologous recombination-proficient tumors, especially CCNE1-amplified cancers, which remain therapeutically intractable. item.title: Shared cortical morphometry and molecular signatures across depression and physical diseases
item.description: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is highly comorbid with physical diseases, suggesting shared neurobiological mechanisms. However, the common structural and molecular substrates underlying this comorbidity remain poorly understood. item.title: Spatial polarization of endothelial ICAM-1 governs T-cell exclusion in melanoma
item.description: An immunosuppressive microenvironment limits therapeutic efficacy in melanoma. Beyond T-cell abundance and function, tumor control depends on T-cell access to malignant cells, yet the vascular mechanisms governing T-cell positioning remain poorly defined. Using RNA sequencing of endothelial cells from tumor cores versus peripheries in a mouse melanoma model, we identified intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1) as a candidate regulator of T-cell localization. During tumor growth, T cells...

item.title: Circumstances of fall-related fracture events among men in late life
item.description: CONCLUSION: Most clinical fracture events in late-life men are fall-related, due to minimal trauma, occur indoors and when activity level is normal or less. Findings suggest that fracture prevention research in this patient group should prioritize evaluation of interventions that may reduce the risk of indoor falls.

item.title: Multi-immersion oblique plane microscope (miOPM): a reconfigurable platform for high-resolution light-sheet fluorescence microscopy
item.description: Light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) enables gentle, rapid and efficient volumetric imaging of biological specimens. Despite its potential, LSFM has fragmented into multiple variants, each narrowly optimized for specific samples or imaging regimes, limiting its broad applicability. Here we introduce the multi-immersion oblique plane microscope (miOPM), an adaptable LSFM platform for high-resolution imaging ranging from subcellular dynamics to whole organisms and cleared tissues. miOPM...

item.title: Predicting long-term survival in primary myelofibrosis
item.description: We interrogated data from 217 subjects with primary myelofibrosis (PMF) diagnosed before 2001 to identify covariates at diagnosis associated with long-term survival. Forty-one survived more than 25 years. Long-term survivors were more often female, younger than 50 years and less likely to have anemia, splenomegaly, increased blood CD34-positive cells, a JAK2^(V617F) variant, and more likely to have grade-0 bone marrow fibrosis and increased platelets. In multivariable logistic regression...

item.title: Targeting the mitochondrial complex I subunit NDUFS2 potentiates FLT3 inhibition in acute myeloid leukaemia with FLT3 internal tandem duplication
item.description: Acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) with FLT3 internal tandem duplication (FLT3-ITD) frequently relapses after FLT3 tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy, highlighting the need to define mechanisms of drug tolerance. Here, we identify the mitochondrial complex I core subunit NDUFS2 as a determinant of FLT3 TKI tolerance in FLT3-ITD AML. item.description: Endocytosis regulates receptor trafficking and signaling, yet its role in colorectal cancer (CRC) remains unclear. We analyzed transcriptomic data from 15,025 CRC tumors to evaluate gene expression in clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME) and the endosomal sorting complexes required for transport (ESCRT) pathway. Pathway-level signatures were compared across consensus molecular subtypes (CMS) and examined in relation to oncogenic signaling programs, while individual endocytosis-related genes were...

item.title: QQ-Based Oxygen Extraction Fraction (OEF) Mapping in Mouse Brain: Initial Experience
item.description: CONCLUSION: This first application of the QQ method in the mouse brain demonstrates its feasibility for spatially resolved OEF quantification and lays the groundwork for future studies investigating oxygen metabolism in animal models.

item.title: Functional characterization of TmToll-6 in mediating innate immune responses to systemic microbial infections in Tenebrio molitor
item.description: Toll-like receptors (TLRs) are evolutionarily conserved regulators of innate immunity and extensively characterized in mammals and Drosophila melanogaster; however, their functional roles in other insects remain incompletely defined. In this study, we investigated the immunological function of TmToll-6 in Tenebrio molitor larvae under systemic pathogenic bacterial and fungal challenge. Transcriptional analyses revealed that its expression was strongly induced in the fat body, gut, Malpighian...

item.title: Ganglioneuroma of the sacral canal: an unusual location with MR imaging findings
item.description: Ganglioneuroma is a rare, benign, slow-growing tumor arising from embryonic neural crest cells that differentiate into the sympathetic ganglia. Accordingly, it can occur anywhere along the sympathetic chain, from the clivus to the sacrum, although it is seen most commonly in the mediastinum, retroperitoneum, adrenal glands, and neck. Although involvement at the sacral level is uncommon, ganglioneuroma typically arises from the anterior surface of the sacrum, with presacral lesions occasionally...

item.title: Interface-driven boost in the performance and stability of protonic ceramic electrochemical cells
item.description: Interfacial resistance remains a key challenge in developing high-performance and durable protonic ceramic electrochemical cells (PCECs), especially at low temperatures. Here, we present a systematic interface engineering strategy that quantitatively correlates interfacial contact coverage with electrochemical performance. A thin and dense PrBa(0.5)Sr(0.5)Co(1.5)Fe(0.5)O(5+δ) interlayer is fabricated via low-cost and scalable precursor-based electrostatic spray deposition on a...

item.title: Injectable hyaluronic acid hydrogels via Diels-Alder and inverse electron demand Diels-Alder click chemistry for drug delivery: A comparative in vitro and in vivo evaluation
item.description: Bio-orthogonal click chemistry enables injectable hydrogels for localized drug delivery with reduced systemic exposure. The crosslinking reaction and resulting network characteristics critically influence the physicochemical and biological performance of hydrogels, necessitating comparative evaluation for rational design. This study compares two hyaluronic acid (HA) hydrogel systems based on furan-maleimide Diels-Alder (DA) and tetrazine-norbornene Inverse Electron Demand Diels-Alder (IEDDA)...

item.title: Heterogeneity in Time-Outcome Associations After Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Binational Registry Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: The association between EVT timing and functional outcome varies according to stroke etiology and clinical characteristics, highlighting heterogeneity in time-outcome relationships among EVT-treated patients and providing observational insight into outcome variability in extended treatment windows.

item.title: Rapid screening of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in port sediments using multiblock spectroscopy and hierarchical classification
item.description: Marine petroleum hydrocarbon contamination remains a persistent concern in port environments, where polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) can accumulate in sediments and pose long-term ecological risks. However, routine PAH assessment relies on labor-intensive laboratory analyses, which can restrict monitoring frequency and spatial coverage. item.description: Antifouling paint additives in surface sediments were investigated in Okpo Harbor and Onsan Harbor, South Korea, two harbors characterized by contrasting dominant anthropogenic activities. Okpo Harbor is a shipbuilding-oriented harbor with a large shipyard, whereas Onsan Harbor represents a multi-use industrial harbor. Organotin compounds were detected at substantial levels in both harbors; however, their spatial distributions and compositional characteristics differed markedly. Okpo Harbor...

item.description: Heavy metal contamination in coastal marine sediments poses significant ecological and public health risks, necessitating the development of efficient and reliable monitoring methods. This study developed a simple, high-throughput approach for monitoring heavy metal pollution in wet sediments using field portable X-ray fluorescence (pXRF) spectrometry. item.title: Mechanical Stress Induces Nuclear Envelope Rupture in Melanoma Cells to Reorganize Tumor-Stromal Interactions
item.description: Growth-induced solid stress and fluid pressure contribute to tumor progression and drug resistance. Beyond tumor endogenous physical forces, cells in the tumor microenvironment may also experience external macroscopic mechanical stress, and some tumors preferentially develop in weight-bearing regions with higher focal pressure. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: VITAL-MD will provide the first large-scale, multicenter randomized evidence evaluating whether an AI-EWS, deployed as a stand-alone device in external validation environments and benchmarked against real-world standard-of-care practice, improves patient-centered outcomes for general-ward patients, advancing the evaluation of AI-SaMD from retrospective diagnostic accuracy toward prospective, action-anchored clinical utility.

item.title: Wire-sealed atomic gas cells for noble-gas nuclear magnetic resonance applications
item.description: We fabricate a wire-sealed atomic gas cell and evaluate its advantages over a conventional torch-sealed cell for noble-gas nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) applications. Wire sealing is performed by sweeping a resistively heated wire across a long stem tube at a constant speed. This approach adapts a previously reported technique for dividing a prefilled vapor cell into smaller cells. In our implementation, an XYZ translation stage precisely controls the wire motion. item.description: Age-related sarcopenia is a condition characterized by a decline in muscle strength and physical function with aging, and its improvement is important given its close association with falls, fractures, and mortality. item.description: CONCLUSION: This trial will provide comparative effectiveness and safety evidence for ultrasound-guided pharmacopuncture added to lifestyle management and exercise education in patients with carpal tunnel syndrome.

item.description: Severe mental illness (SMI) often limits participation in traditional therapy due to motivational and cognitive deficits. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Five-day post-EVT hyperglycemic status was independently associated with worse 3-month functional outcomes beyond chronic glycemic burden, supporting re-evaluation of targeted glycemic interventions during this vulnerable window.

item.title: Temporal Trends in the Distribution of Extracranial Carotid and Intracranial Artery Disease Among South Korean Stroke Patients
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In South Korean patients with anterior-circulation steno-occlusive ischemic stroke, symptomatic ECAD has declined over 16 years, contrasting with the persistently high burden of IAD. Further research is needed to clarify what caused these trends.

item.title: Net carbon losses in Central African forests revealed by high-resolution biomass change maps
item.description: Dense humid forests in Central Africa hold vast biomass carbon stocks but are increasingly affected by small-scale disturbances that are difficult to detect with current satellite observations. Here, we generate 10 m canopy height maps for 2019-2022 using deep learning with spaceborne lidar and Sentinel-1/-2 imagery, and derive aboveground biomass changes at 30 m resolution. item.description: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a highly heritable psychiatric disorder. An increasing number of whole-exome sequencing (WES) studies have been conducted on psychiatric research. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The number of patients receiving HA eye drops increased without significant trend, whereas total prescription quantity rose by three-quarters, with increased supply per patient, marked shift toward unit-dose formulations, and growth concentrated among long-term users. item.title: From singular jets to compound droplets: Viscosity and inertia control of immiscible drop-pool impact dynamics
item.description: HYPOTHESIS: Secondary-droplet composition in immiscible drop-pool impact is hypothesized to be governed by the relative motion of the oil-air and oil-water interfaces formed at the tip and inside the jet, respectively. Increasing oil (droplet) viscosity should reduce this relative motion and favor compound oil-water droplets, while crown breakup may provide an additional high-inertia route to their formation.
